title: source_commit_of decides dirty tree-wide, so a whiteboard edit stamps every estate THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT
body:
# 0033: source_commit_of decides dirty tree-wide, so a whiteboard edit stamps every estate THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT

## Tags

install, manifest, provenance, whiteboard, false-signal

## Summary

`source_commit_of` decides the manifest's dirty stamp with a TREE-WIDE `git status --porcelain`, but the manifest it stamps describes only the vendored surface -- `bin/devbin` plus the lib tree, every file of it in the manifest. So any dirty path OUTSIDE that surface makes the stamp assert `+dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT` about bytes that match HEAD exactly.

## Reproduction

Observed by devbin/vc during fleet sweep #6 (devbin runtime `37ce21f5` -> `93e0cb7`, eleven vendored installs, on hv's go). A single open whiteboard board -- `intent/whiteboard/cc/wip.md`, a header edit -- was the only dirty path in the tree. At that moment:

- `git status --porcelain` -- non-empty, so every estate's manifest stamped `+dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT`.
- `git status --porcelain -- lib bin` -- empty. The vendored bytes provably matched `93e0cb7`.

Eleven trees carried the degraded stamp, and that is the record the NEXT sweep reads.

## Root Cause

`lib/install:245`, inside `source_commit_of`. It is the only `--porcelain` call in the tree, so the class has exactly one site.

The tree-wide predicate is not an oversight -- the function's header comment is explicit that DIRTY IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN, because a sha read from a dirty source describes bytes no commit has. That reasoning is correct and is not what is being questioned. What is wrong is the SCOPE of "dirty": the question the manifest asks is what the VENDORED bytes correspond to outside themselves, and a non-vendored file cannot change the answer.

## Impact

It errs safe -- over-reports dirty, never under-reports clean -- so it blocks nothing and misleads nobody who reads it carefully. Severity is low for that reason.

The cost is slower. In a project with a live whiteboard the source tree is almost never clean, because some node is always mid-edit; so the accurate stamp is close to UNREACHABLE exactly where the fleet record matters most. A check that is correct in principle and unsatisfiable in practice gets read as noise, and then it stops being read at all.

That is the same failure mode as issue 0030, arriving from the opposite direction. 0030 was a guard that printed nothing when absent, so silence read as pass. This prints a warning so reliably that the warning stops carrying information. Both end with a signal nobody can act on.

## Proposed Fix

**THE FIX FILED HERE WAS WRONG, AND IT IS LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPLACED.** It read:

> Narrow the predicate to devbin's own half, enumerated through the functions that already exist: `vendored_paths` for the list, `vendor_source_path` for the source-side mapping.

That builds a git pathspec out of a FILE LIST, and `vendored_paths` enumerates with `find`. A vendored file deleted but not yet committed therefore stops being listed, git is asked only about the names that survived, and the answer is CLEAN over a missing file. That is an UNDER-report of clean -- the one direction this issue's own Impact section says the subsystem must never go. Measured on a fixture with `lib/beta` removed:

| predicate                                     | answer with `lib/beta` deleted |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| file list from `vendored_paths`               | CLEAN                          |
| directory scope                               | ` D lib/beta`                  |

The refused `-- lib bin` shape from the original report was refused on Highlander grounds and was never unsafe. The replacement written here was unsafe. Both were reasoned rather than run.

## Resolution -- FIXED

**`vendored_scope <srcroot>`**, new in `lib/install`, third member of the `vendored_paths` / `vendored_dir_files` family and separate from them for the same stated reason those two are separate: it answers a different question. `vendored_paths` asks WHICH FILES ship, `vendored_dir_files` asks what is ON DISK, `vendored_scope` asks WHERE devbin's half lives -- the only shape a git pathspec can take. It emits `$srcroot/bin/devbin` and whatever `devbin_lib_dir` resolves, so the runtime location still has exactly one source of truth.

`source_commit_of` asks `git status --porcelain` against that scope. **When the half cannot be located it asks the tree-wide question instead**, rather than inventing a narrower one -- a root with no `lib/` and no `bin/.devbin/lib/` is not a devbin source this can clear, and absent must never be readable as clean. That fallback is also what keeps the four pre-existing `source_commit` tests meaningful: their fixture has no seam at all.

## Verification -- ALL ARMS DRIVEN RED FIRST

A probe built the same source in seven states and ran `source_commit_of` over each, before and after. Only one row moved:

| state                                      | before   | after    |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- |
| clean                                      | CLEAN    | CLEAN    |
| **non-vendored file modified (the defect)**| **DIRTY**| **CLEAN**|
| vendored file modified                     | DIRTY    | DIRTY    |
| vendored file DELETED                      | DIRTY    | DIRTY    |
| vendored file added, untracked             | DIRTY    | DIRTY    |
| `bin/devbin` modified                      | DIRTY    | DIRTY    |
| repo with no devbin surface at all, dirty  | DIRTY    | DIRTY    |

Six tests were added or retargeted, and each was then proven to FAIL against a deliberately broken implementation -- a green test proves nothing until it has been watched go red:

| mutation applied to the fix                 | went red                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| scope emits the file list, not the directory| `source_commit still stamps a DELETED file inside the seam`, and NOTHING ELSE in 648 tests |
| scope forced empty, ie the tree-wide defect | `source_commit ignores a dirty file OUTSIDE the seam` plus the vendor-level twin |

The deletion arm being the ONLY red in 648 tests under the first mutation is the point of it: no other test in the suite can see that failure.

`tests/unit/vendor.bats` had one test asserting the OLD behaviour deliberately, with a written rationale -- it dirtied a non-vendored file so the tree would be level, and asserted `Level with` and `MATCH NO COMMIT` together. That pairing is no longer reachable and should not be. It was SPLIT rather than deleted: what was right in it (a bare sha beside a verdict read off the working tree is a confident false statement) now aims at a vendored file, where the working tree really does differ from HEAD; the second half is the 0033 regression guard.

Suite green: `test bats` rc=0 with a 0-byte verdict seal, `check all` rc=0.

## Related

- 0030 -- a whiteboard guard whose absence printed nothing. Same end state, opposite mechanism.
- Reported by devbin/vc during fleet sweep #6; diagnosis confirmed independently against `lib/install` before filing.
- `intent/llm/LESSONS.md` -- a fix proposed at diagnosis time inherits the diagnosis's authority without its evidence.
- `usage-rules.md` -- the seam-scoped dirty question, and never building a pathspec from a `find` list.
